name: Orla March
life: “I still remember a hand taking mine in an ambulance queue.” On Monday, near Breakwater Way, Orla stops on the landward side of the cycle track to watch the first boats turn for home.
voice: I iron for the young man opposite because he held my hand when the ambulance took my wife.
appearance: Orla is easy to recognize by a long silver braid and a crooked front tooth visible when laughing. Usually dressed in a gray fisher's sweater with a pressed flower kept in the clear back of a phone case, Orla draws small circles on a tabletop while waiting when listening.
personality: Orla has excellent recall for voices and a poor memory for official titles. Someone who waited patiently at a counter years ago is more likely to be remembered than the person in charge.
agenda: To finish a clean shirt for the bereaved neighbor.
family: Chris Valdez is Orla’s first cousin once removed. Orla offers the first invitation. Chris gets to change the plan. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *The free fringe*, Chris says, “I timed the conversation like a normal trim.”
connections: Jorge Nash (owner of the pressed shirt). A grateful customer tries to pay the neighbor who irons the stranger's shirt.

reactions.situation: A staff supervisor demands the stranger's laundry back
reactions.response: Orla checks with the shirt's owner before handing it over to anyone else.

reactions.situation: An envelope of wages is found under a café chair
reactions.response: Orla finds a second person to witness its return so an honest mistake won't cost a worker their pay.
